Eliashib
eh-LY-ah-shib
proper noun
Hebrew elyashib, “God restores” or “whom God restores,” the high priest in Nehemiah’s day who built the sheep gate but compromised by lodging Tobiah in the temple courts.

📖 Biblical Definition

Eliashib was the high priest in the days of Nehemiah, who with his brethren the priests rose up and built the sheep gate, sanctified it, and set up its doors, leading the great work of rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem (Neh 3:1). To begin the labour, and at the holy gate by which the sacrifices entered, was honour indeed. Yet the same Eliashib, being allied unto Tobiah the Ammonite, that enemy of God’s people who had mocked and resisted the building, prepared for him a great chamber in the courts of the house of God, in the very place where the offerings and the tithes had been laid up (Neh 13:4-5). When Nehemiah returned and learned of the evil, he cast forth all Tobiah’s household stuff out of the chamber and cleansed it (Neh 13:7-9,28). The dictionary honours the building of the sheep gate but will not hide the compromise, for here is a sober warning of the unequal yoke. The high priest, whose name means “God restores,” gave a chamber in the temple to the very foe of the temple, mingling the holy with the profane through alliance with the ungodly. Eliashib stands as a witness that a man may begin a good work and yet corrupt it by friendship with the enemies of God; and he calls every steward of holy things to be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers, lest the courts of the LORD be defiled.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The high priest in Nehemiah’s day who built the sheep gate but lodged Tobiah the Ammonite in the temple courts.

ELIASHIB, the high priest in the days of Nehemiah, signifying “God restores.”

He with the priests built the sheep gate and sanctified it.

Being allied to Tobiah the Ammonite, he gave him a chamber in the temple courts.

Nehemiah cast out Tobiah’s stuff and cleansed the chamber on his return.

It witnesses both to good labour begun and to the corruption of an unequal yoke.

📖 Key Scripture

Neh 3:1 — "Then Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brethren the priests, and they builded the sheep gate; they sanctified it, and set up the doors of it; even unto the tower of Meah they sanctified it, unto the tower of Hananeel."

Neh 13:7 — "And I came to Jerusalem, and understood of the evil that Eliashib did for Tobiah, in preparing him a chamber in the courts of the house of God."

Neh 13:9 — "Then I commanded, and they cleansed the chambers: and thither brought I again the vessels of the house of God, with the meat offering and the frankincense."

2Co 6:14 — "Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

His building was good, but Eliashib’s alliance with Tobiah is a true warning against the unequal yoke that defiles the house of God.

expand to see more

Eliashib the high priest is honoured for rising up to build the sheep gate, the first labour named in the rebuilding of the wall; and the dictionary will not strip him of that honour. Yet his is not the caveat of an obscure name untouched by controversy, for the Scripture itself names his fault, that the reader may learn from it. The high priest who began the wall ended by giving the enemy of the wall a room within the holy courts.

The corruption to avoid is the unequal yoke that mingles the holy with the profane. Eliashib, whose name means “God restores,” was allied unto Tobiah the Ammonite, the very man who had laughed the builders to scorn, and lodged him where the tithes of the LORD had been stored. So a good work was defiled by friendship with the ungodly, until Nehemiah cast the stuff forth and cleansed the place. The LORD warns every steward of His house: be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers, for the courts of God are not to be let out to His enemies, and the church that befriends the world betrays the trust of her Lord.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “God restores,” Eliashib names the high priest who built the sheep gate but compromised with Tobiah.

expand to see more

Eliashib — Hebrew elyashib, “God restores” or “whom God restores.”

He was the high priest in the days of Nehemiah.

He with the priests built and sanctified the sheep gate.

He gave Tobiah the Ammonite a chamber in the courts of the house of God.

His grandson married the daughter of Sanballat and was chased away by Nehemiah.

Usage

"Like Eliashib, a man may begin a good work and yet defile it by friendship with the enemies of God."

"The sheep gate well built cannot excuse a chamber given to Tobiah in the courts of the LORD."

"Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers, lest the holy house be let out to its foes."
